title: The Atmos clock
content_html:
1929–1932

1929–1932

The Reut­ter Clock

In 1930 the pro­duc­tion of the first Reut­ter wat­ches star­ted, the forerun­ners of the Atmos watch. The­re were about 24 dif­fe­rent models from 1932–34, the first Reut­ter wat­ches were still equip­ped with the “Clu­ses“ movement—with only 4 rubies, the rest of the pivots were steel. From 1932/33 on, a new move­ment cali­ber 30′‘A was used, equip­ped with 15 rubies. Howe­ver, the main dif­fe­rence from the later Atmos watch was main­ly the mer­cu­ry-based motor, which trans­mit­ted the tem­pe­ra­tu­re fluc­tua­tions of the atmo­sphe­re to the main­spring bar­rel. From 1936, deve­lo­p­ment began on a new motor prin­ci­ple, as the dan­gers of mer­cu­ry beca­me known and the motor con­s­truct was very fra­gi­le, the­r­e­fo­re dif­fi­cult to transport.

1939–1950

1939–1950

ATMOS II

The first “real“ Atmos clock, powered by a gas-fil­led metal bel­low, was deve­lo­ped in 1935–38. The move­ment was fur­ther deve­lo­ped and a new case with glass discs was desi­gned. The typi­cal design, which remain­ed until the ear­ly 1990s, was crea­ted. Over the years, the­re were minor chan­ges to the design, such as the adjus­t­ment knob which points back­wards to the pres­su­re box, or for­wards, towards the dial. The pla­te shows the Gen­e­va finish, which is still com­mon today. The Atmos II was sold from 1939 on and went into seri­al pro­duc­tion for the first time. The myth of the per­pe­tu­al moti­on machi­ne was created.

1948–1955

1948–1955

Cali­ber 519

ATMOS III

With the cali­ber 519, fur­ther minor chan­ges were made. The fine adjus­t­ment was revi­sed and pla­ced cen­tral­ly at the front over the dial, the pla­te width is redu­ced and the con­s­truc­tion of the case is some­what simplified—overall, the watch beco­mes more sui­ta­ble for mass pro­duc­tion. The move­ment remains most­ly unch­an­ged. The num­ber of wat­ches pro­du­ced increased from 2,000 in 1948 to 10,000 by 1951.

1953–1966

1953–1966

Cali­ber 522 and 532

Spe­cial series ATMOS IV

The cali­ber 522 and 532 were spe­cial models that were pro­du­ced only brief­ly and are con­side­red inter­me­dia­te models. Today, the cali­ber 522 is often cal­led “Tuxe­do“ becau­se of the pro­mi­nent front door, which is deco­ra­ted with the striking Gen­e­va cut. The cali­ber 532 dif­fers only slight­ly from the cali­ber 526, here the case front was reinter­pre­ted and given a new design. This model was pro­du­ced only in small numbers.

1955–1984

1955–1984

Cali­ber 526

Atmos V

The seri­al pro­duc­tion of the Atmos clock con­ti­nues with the cali­ber 526. The con­s­truc­tion of a new move­ment allows the pro­duc­tion of 1,500 Atmos clocks per month, the clock is pre­sen­ted in Switz­er­land as a sta­te gift, in the U.S. very often as a cor­po­ra­te gift for employees to cele­bra­te an anni­ver­sa­ry. The­r­e­fo­re, this model is also often found engra­ved or with a glued plaque on the front. Abo­ve men­tio­ned cali­ber 519 and 522 are pro­du­ced in par­al­lel and, howe­ver, are in dis­con­ti­nua­tion. The cali­ber 526 its­elf dif­fers main­ly by smal­ler dimen­si­ons, which also gives it the nick­na­me “Baby Atmos“. The case was modi­fied, the pen­dulum latch is loca­ted insi­de under the dial—no lon­ger under the case back. Fur­ther­mo­re, the clock no lon­ger has a glass cover, which is remo­va­ble, but a small door, which can be ope­ned with a gold-pla­ted brass but­ton. The move­ment is built into this clas­sic watch case, but also in spe­cial ver­si­ons of the coming deca­des. For exam­p­le, in the model Atmos Ven­do­me and Atmos Ven­do­me Paris.

1958–1968

1958–1968

Cali­ber 528

Atmos VI

Here, the lar­ger ori­gi­nal model of the Atmos clock is revi­ved. The suc­cess of the brand leads to the launch of even more models. The old dimen­si­ons are com­bi­ned with the new advan­ced move­ment and slim­mer pla­tes. The watch has initi­al­ly a hood like the Atmos II and Atmos III, which is chan­ged to a front door with a small pusher in the fol­lo­wing models from Atmos VIII. Unfort­u­na­te­ly, we have no offi­ci­al infor­ma­ti­on about the pro­duc­tion peri­od, but our records sug­gest that this model was pro­du­ced as ear­ly as 1958.

1967–1984

1967–1984

Cali­ber 526, 528, 528/1 ff.

Atmos VIII

Par­al­lel to the abo­ve-men­tio­ned cali­bers, the Atmos VIII, cali­ber 528/1 is added to the cata­logs in 1967. First used in the Embas­sy model, the cali­ber beco­mes the new series pro­duc­tion. At first, this model is still sold with a hood (Atmos VI), like the pre­vious vari­ants, later on, it is chan­ged to a front door (Atmos VIII). The case pro­por­ti­ons are again lar­ger, the move­ment can be adjus­ted and regu­la­ted through a remo­va­ble front dial. Again, the­re are dif­fe­rent dial vari­ants and some spe­cial edi­ti­ons like the Atmos “fan­ta­sy models“ (desi­gned by Lui­gi Cola­ni, in cata­logs 1974/75). It is said that this cali­ber is the most built cali­ber of the Atmos watch until today.

bis 1983

bis 1983

Spe­cial edi­ti­ons until 1983

Limi­t­ed editions

Spe­cial men­ti­on should be made of various spe­cial edi­ti­ons of the Atmos clock, which have been pro­du­ced again and again in small pro­duc­tion runs, most­ly for various com­pa­ny anni­ver­s­a­ries. The­se include, for exam­p­le, the Atmos Jubi­lee, the Atmos Pres­ti­ge (and later the Atmos Ope­ra). Mar­king the fif­tieth anni­ver­sa­ry of the Atmos clock, con­tem­po­ra­ry tech­no­lo­gy is here inser­ted into the ori­gi­nal pro­to­ty­pe design of the Reut­ter wat­ches (1930s). In a limi­t­ed edi­ti­on of 1,500 to 3,000 pie­ces, the­se models con­ti­nue to enjoy gre­at popu­la­ri­ty today. Espe­ci­al­ly the detail­ed design with face­ted discs and lar­ge screwed balan­ce weights testi­fies to the flair of the past era.

1983–2000

1983–2000

Cali­ber 540a

The rede­sign of a classic

From 1983, the cali­ber 540, which had been com­ple­te­ly over­hau­led in design, was lis­ted in the cata­logs. The focus was on a slim­mer design and modi­fied pro­por­ti­ons in detail. Tech­ni­cal­ly, the move­ment was com­ple­te­ly rebuilt: The move­ment pla­te, the pen­dulum sus­pen­si­on, and all gears were com­ple­te­ly rede­si­gned. Also, the main­spring bar­rel was moved and, for the first time, a moon pha­se was possible—and that wit­hout an extra gear! This was the first “com­pli­ca­ti­on“ of the Atmos watch, the so-cal­led cali­ber 544—a mile­stone. In the begin­ning, this cali­ber is also equip­ped with a tem­pe­ra­tu­re and hygro­me­ter. Not visi­ble from the out­side, but of gre­at importance: The manu­fac­tu­ring pro­cess of the pres­su­re box, the heart of every Atmos clock, was fun­da­men­tal­ly revi­sed. The gas-fil­led metal bel­lows, which react very sen­si­tively to any chan­ge in tem­pe­ra­tu­re, have now been manu­fac­tu­red using an indus­tri­al plas­ma wel­ding pro­cess, which great­ly extends its ser­vice life and thus helps the Atmos watch to last even lon­ger. Dif­fe­rent models, dials, and cali­ber vari­ants were introduced.

1985–2003

1985–2003

Cali­ber 540ff.

Spe­cial models

In addi­ti­on to various case varia­ti­ons, dif­fe­rent design varia­ti­ons have mana­ged to get a spe­cial place. Dif­fe­rent vari­ants such as the Atmos Ope­ra or the Atmos Fon­taine­bleau in a woo­den case are issued and cau­se a sen­sa­ti­on. First and fore­most, the Atmos Atlantis/3000, desi­gned in 1995 by the desi­gner KOH­LER et REKOW in Paris, was the trend­set­ting design that car­ri­es the Atmos watch in a glass tra­pe­ze on 3 lar­ge poin­ted metal cones. Dif­fe­rent ver­si­ons, in gold or rho­di­um pla­ted, were pro­du­ced in small num­bers. A mas­ter­pie­ce of tech­no­lo­gy and almost uni­que in watch histo­ry is the “Atmos Atlan­tis du Mil­len­aire“ which is equip­ped with a per­pe­tu­al moon, month, and year calen­dar. A snail-shaped dial with a sepa­ra­te hand move­ment shows the years from 2000 AD to 3000 AD. A watch that car­ri­es the thought “until all eternity“.
The­re are also spe­cial edi­ti­ons of this vari­ant, such as the Atmos du Mil­len­aire Mar­que­te­rie (cali­ber 546). A luxu­rious­ly hand­craf­ted wal­nut case with intri­ca­te inlay work unders­cores the spe­cial natu­re of this watch.

2003–Today

2003–Today

Cali­ber 560ff. The new mill­en­ni­um also ushe­red in a new era for the Atmos watch. The cali­ber 540 was dis­con­tin­ued and the cali­ber 560 was lis­ted in dif­fe­rent vari­ants in the cata­logs. Main­ly design adjus­t­ments were made. Howe­ver, the Atmos clock with moon pha­se (form­er­ly cali­ber 544, now cali­ber 562) was equip­ped with ano­ther com­pli­ca­ti­on: a month­ly calendar–as first seen on the Atmos du Millenaire.

2003–Today

2003–Today

Cali­ber 560ff..

Spe­cial variants

Here, too, spe­cial model varia­ti­ons were crea­ted. Par­ti­cu­lar­ly note­wor­t­hy, for exam­p­le, is the model Atmos Trans­pa­ren­te, in which the Atmos clock is sus­pen­ded in a glass cube. This model was pro­du­ced in dif­fe­rent ver­si­ons, without/with moon pha­se dis­play, even in a “du Mil­len­aire“ variant—with a 1,000-year calen­dar page.

2008–Today

2008–Today

Atmos Marc Newson

Spe­cial variants

A sepa­ra­te room should still get the Atmos clock models around Marc News­on. In 2008, coope­ra­ti­on began bet­ween the desi­gner and Jae­ger-LeCoult­re that con­ti­nues to this day. Only a few dif­fe­rent designs have been rea­li­zed sin­ce then, but all with very distinc­ti­ve designs and extre­me­ly exqui­si­te cases. Ori­gi­nal­ly Marc News­on was com­mis­sio­ned to design an Atmos watch for the 80th anni­ver­sa­ry of the same, so today in 2022 the­re is alre­a­dy the third model desi­gned by News­on to buy.

blocks.html_en: From 1983, the cali­ber 540, which had been com­ple­te­ly over­hau­led in design, was lis­ted in the cata­logs. The focus was on a slim­mer design and modi­fied pro­por­ti­ons in detail. Tech­ni­cal­ly, the move­ment was com­ple­te­ly rebuilt: The move­ment pla­te, the pen­dulum sus­pen­si­on, and all gears were com­ple­te­ly rede­si­gned. Also, the main­spring bar­rel was moved and, for the first time, a moon pha­se was possible—and that wit­hout an extra gear! This was the first “com­pli­ca­ti­on“ of the Atmos watch, the so-cal­led cali­ber 544—a mile­stone. In the begin­ning, this cali­ber is also equip­ped with a tem­pe­ra­tu­re and hygro­me­ter. Not visi­ble from the out­side, but of gre­at importance: The manu­fac­tu­ring pro­cess of the pres­su­re box, the heart of every Atmos clock, was fun­da­men­tal­ly revi­sed. The gas-fil­led metal bel­lows, which react very sen­si­tively to any chan­ge in tem­pe­ra­tu­re, have now been manu­fac­tu­red using an indus­tri­al plas­ma wel­ding pro­cess, which great­ly extends its ser­vice life and thus helps the Atmos watch to last even lon­ger. Dif­fe­rent models, dials, and cali­ber vari­ants were introduced.

blocks.html_en:
In addi­ti­on to various case varia­ti­ons, dif­fe­rent design varia­ti­ons have mana­ged to get a spe­cial place. Dif­fe­rent vari­ants such as the Atmos Ope­ra or the Atmos Fon­taine­bleau in a woo­den case are issued and cau­se a sen­sa­ti­on. First and fore­most, the Atmos Atlantis/3000, desi­gned in 1995 by the desi­gner KOH­LER et REKOW in Paris, was the trend­set­ting design that car­ri­es the Atmos watch in a glass tra­pe­ze on 3 lar­ge poin­ted metal cones. Dif­fe­rent ver­si­ons, in gold or rho­di­um pla­ted, were pro­du­ced in small num­bers. A mas­ter­pie­ce of tech­no­lo­gy and almost uni­que in watch histo­ry is the “Atmos Atlan­tis du Mil­len­aire“ which is equip­ped with a per­pe­tu­al moon, month, and year calen­dar. A snail-shaped dial with a sepa­ra­te hand move­ment shows the years from 2000 AD to 3000 AD. A watch that car­ri­es the thought “until all eternity“.
The­re are also spe­cial edi­ti­ons of this vari­ant, such as the Atmos du Mil­len­aire Mar­que­te­rie (cali­ber 546). A luxu­rious­ly hand­craf­ted wal­nut case with intri­ca­te inlay work unders­cores the spe­cial natu­re of this watch.

content_html_zh:
1929–1932

1929–1932

路透社时钟

1930 年，第一批 Reutter 手表开始生产，这是 Atmos 手表的前身。 从 1932 年到 34 年，大约有 24 种不同的型号，第一批 Reutter 手表仍然配备“Cluses”机芯——只有 4 颗红宝石，其余的枢轴都是钢制的。 从1932/33年开始，使用了新的30''A机芯，配备15颗红宝石。 然而，与后来的Atmos手表的主要区别主要在于水银马达，它将大气的温度波动传输到主发条盒。 从 1936 年开始，随着汞的危险性逐渐为人所知，并且电机结构非常脆弱，因此难以运输，人们开始开发新的电机原理。

1939–1950

1939–1950

大气二号

第一个“真正的”Atmos 时钟于 1935-38 年开发，由充气金属波纹管提供动力。 该机芯得到进一步开发，并设计了带有玻璃圆盘的新表壳。 典型的设计一直延续到 20 世纪 90 年代初。 多年来，设计发生了一些细微的变化，例如调节旋钮向后指向压力盒，或向前指向表盘。 表盘采用日内瓦饰面，至今仍很常见。 Atmos II 从 1939 年开始销售，并首次进入批量生产。 永动机的神话就此诞生。

1948–1955

1948–1955

Cali­ber 519

大气三世

519 机芯还进行了进一步的细微改动。 微调装置经过修改，置于表盘正面中央，板宽减小，表壳结构也有所简化——总体而言，腕表变得更适合批量生产。 运动基本保持不变。 手表的生产数量从 1948 年的 2,000 只增加到 1951 年的 10,000 只。

1953–1966

1953–1966

机芯 522 和 532

特别系列 ATMOS IV

522 和 532 机芯是特殊型号，仅短暂生产，被视为中间型号。 如今，522 机芯经常被称为“Tuxedo”，因为其突出的前门饰有引人注目的日内瓦切割。 532 机芯与 526 机芯仅略有不同，表壳正面经过重新诠释并采用全新设计。 该型号仅少量生产。

1955–1984

1955–1984

Cali­ber 526

全景声V

Atmos 时钟的系列生产继续采用 526 机芯。 新机芯的构造允许每月生产 1,500 个 Atmos 时钟，该时钟在瑞士作为国礼赠送，在美国则经常作为公司员工庆祝周年纪念的礼物。 因此，该模型的正面也经常出现雕刻或胶合牌匾。 上述 519 和 522 机芯是并行生产的，但已停产。 526 机芯本身的主要区别在于较小的尺寸，这也使其获得了“Baby Atmos”的绰号。 表壳经过修改，摆锤锁位于表盘下方，不再位于表背下方。 此外，时钟不再有一个可拆卸的玻璃盖，而是一个小门，可以用镀金黄铜按钮打开。 该机芯内置于这款经典表壳中，但也出现在未来几十年的特殊版本中。 例如，Atmos Vendome 模型和 Atmos Vendome Paris 模型。

1958–1968

1958–1968

Cali­ber 528

大气六号

在这里，更大的 Atmos 时钟原始模型得到了复兴。 该品牌的成功导致了更多车型的推出。 旧尺寸与新的先进机芯和更纤薄的夹板相结合。 这款手表最初像 Atmos II 和 Atmos III 一样有一个引擎盖，在 Atmos VIII 的以下型号中改为带有小按钮的前门。 不幸的是，我们没有关于生产时期的官方信息，但我们的记录表明该型号早在 1958 年就生产了。

1967–1984

1967–1984

机芯 526、528、528/1 及以上。

八号全景声

与上述机芯并行，Atmos VIII 528/1 机芯于 1967 年添加到产品目录中。 该机芯首次用于Embassy 型号，成为新系列产品。 起初，这款车型与之前的车型一样，仍然是带引擎盖（Atmos VI）出售，后来，它改为带前门（Atmos VIII）。 表壳比例再次变大，机芯可通过可拆卸的前表盘进行调整和调节。 同样，还有不同的表盘变体和一些特别版本，例如 Atmos“幻想型号”（由 Luigi Colani 设计，在 1974/75 年目录中）。 据说，这款机芯是迄今为止Atmos腕表内置最多的机芯。

bis 1983

bis 1983

1983 年之前的特别版

限量版

特别值得一提的是 Atmos 时钟的各种特别版本，这些时钟在小批量生产中一次又一次地生产，主要是为了各种公司周年纪念日。 例如，其中包括 Atmos Jubilee、Atmos Prestige（以及后来的 Atmos Opera）。 为纪念 Atmos 时钟诞生 50 周年，Reutter 手表（1930 年代）的原始原型设计中融入了现代技术。 这些款式限量发行 1,500 至 3,000 枚，至今仍广受欢迎。 尤其是刻面圆盘和大型螺丝平衡配重的详细设计证明了过去时代的才华。

1983–2000

1983–2000

机芯 540a

经典的重新设计

自 1983 年起，设计经过全面革新的 540 机芯被列入目录。 重点是更纤薄的设计和细节上的比例修改。 从技术上讲，机芯经过彻底重建：机芯夹板、摆锤悬架和所有齿轮都经过彻底重新设计。 此外，主发条盒也被移动，并且首次实现了月相显示——而且无需额外的齿轮！ 这是 Atmos 腕表的第一个“复杂功能”，即所谓的 544 机芯，具有里程碑意义。 最初，这款机芯还配备了温度和湿度计。 从外面看不出来，但非常重要：压力盒的制造工艺，每个 Atmos 时钟的核心，都经过了根本性的修改。 充气金属波纹管对温度的任何变化都非常敏感，现在采用工业等离子焊接工艺制造，大大延长了其使用寿命，从而帮助 Atmos 手表使用寿命更长。 推出了不同的型号、表盘和机芯。

1985–2003

1985–2003

口径 540ff。

特殊型号

除了各种表壳变化之外，不同的设计变化也获得了特殊的地位。 不同的版本，如 Atmos Opera 或 Atmos Fontainebleau 木盒发行，并引起轰动。 首先也是最重要的是，Atmos Atlantis/3000 由巴黎设计师 KOHLER et REKOW 于 1995 年设计，是引领潮流的设计，Atmos 手表采用 3 个大尖头金属锥体上的玻璃梯形结构。 小批量生产了不同的镀金或镀铑版本。 “Atmos Atlantis du Millenaire”是腕表历史上独一无二的技术杰作，配备万年历月历、月历和年历。 蜗牛形表盘搭配独立指针机芯，显示公元2000年至公元3000年的年份。 一款承载“直到永恒”理念的腕表。 该型号还有特别版，例如 Atmos du Millenaire Marqueterie（机芯 546）。 奢华的手工胡桃木表壳搭配复杂的镶嵌工艺，凸显了这款腕表的特殊性。

2003–Today

2003–Today

口径 560ff。 新千年也为Atmos腕表迎来了新纪元。 540 机芯已停产，560 机芯在目录中以不同型号列出。 主要是进行了设计调整。 然而，具有月相功能的 Atmos 时钟（之前为 544 机芯，现在为 562 机芯）配备了另一项复杂功能：月历——这首次出现在 Atmos du Millenaire 上。

2003–Today

2003–Today

口径 560ff..

特殊型号

在这里，也创建了特殊的模型变体。 例如，特别值得注意的是Atmos透明模型，其中Atmos时钟悬挂在玻璃立方体中。 该表款有不同版本，有/无月相显示，甚至有“du Millenaire”版本——带有 1,000 年日历页。

2008–Today

2008–Today

马克·纽森

特殊型号

一个单独的房间应该仍然可以放置 Marc Newson 周围的 Atmos 时钟模型。 2008年，设计师与积家开始合作，并持续至今。 此后仅实现了几种不同的设计，但都具有非常独特的设计和极其精美的表壳。 最初，马克·纽森 (Marc Newson) 受委托为 Atmos 腕表设计 80 周年纪念，所以在 2022 年的今天，已经有纽森设计的第三款腕表可供购买。
